webhook.title: Webhook status
webhook.secretHint: Sent in the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header. Telegram never returns it — save it on your server. Empty = no secret.
webhook.maxConnectionsHint: 1–100, default 40. Lower it to reduce load on your server.
webhook.ipHint: Send updates to this IP instead of resolving the domain via DNS.
webhook.certificateHint: Upload the public key (PEM) only if your server uses a self-signed certificate.
webhook.updatesHint: Default = all update types except chat_member, message_reaction and message_reaction_count; those are delivered only when selected explicitly.
webhook.dropHint: Re-sets the current webhook with drop_pending_updates. Enter the secret token again to keep it, otherwise it will be removed. A pinned IP or uploaded certificate is not preserved — use the form above in that case.
webhook.deleteHint: The bot stops receiving updates on the URL and can use getUpdates (long polling) again.

security: Static page hosted on GitHub Pages: there is no server that could store or log your token.
Requests go from your browser straight to api.telegram.org (or to the API server you choose).
The token is kept only in this browser tab unless you tick “Remember on this device”. “Disconnect” removes it.
Strict Content Security Policy, no analytics, no third-party scripts. The source code is open — check it or host your own copy.

faq.q: Is it safe to enter my bot token here?
faq.a: The page is fully static and has no backend. The token is used only in your browser to call the Telegram Bot API and is never sent anywhere else. You can audit the open-source code or run your own copy. If you think a token has leaked, revoke it in @BotFather → /revoke.

faq.q: How do I check my Telegram bot's webhook?
faq.a: Connect the bot and open the Webhook tab. It calls getWebhookInfo and shows the URL, the number of pending updates, the last delivery error with its time and a hint on how to fix it.

faq.q: How do I delete a webhook and switch to getUpdates?
faq.a: Open Webhook → Danger zone → Delete webhook. Optionally drop pending updates. After that the bot can receive updates with getUpdates (long polling) again — otherwise Telegram answers “409 Conflict: can't use getUpdates method while webhook is active”.

faq.q: Why are there pending updates and the bot doesn't answer?
faq.a: Telegram can't deliver updates to your webhook. Look at the last error: SSL problems, DNS errors, timeouts or HTTP 4xx/5xx from your server. Fix the server, then optionally drop the queued updates.
A list of update types the bot receives. By default you get everything except chat_member, message_reaction and message_reaction_count. To receive those, choose the types explicitly.

faq.q: Can I set different commands for groups or other languages?
faq.a: Yes. In the Commands tab choose a scope (all private chats, all groups, administrators, a specific chat or member) and a language. Telegram picks the most specific list for each user.

faq.q: It says “Network error” when I connect. What now?
faq.a: Your network, browser extension or country may block api.telegram.org. Open “Advanced: API server” and use your own proxy (a free Cloudflare Worker template is in the repository) or a local Bot API server.

faq.q: Is it free? Can I host it myself?
faq.a: Yes, it's free and MIT-licensed. Fork the repository and enable GitHub Pages, or run npm run build and upload the dist folder to any static hosting.

setWebhook.title: How to Set a Telegram Bot Webhook Online (setWebhook)
setWebhook.description: Set a Telegram bot webhook in a few clicks: HTTPS URL, secret token, allowed_updates, max_connections and self-signed certificate. With curl examples.
setWebhook.h1: How to set a Telegram bot webhook
setWebhook.lead: A webhook makes Telegram push every update to your HTTPS endpoint instead of you polling getUpdates. Here is how to set it up correctly and securely.
setWebhook.body:
Requirements

  • A public HTTPS URL. Plain HTTP is not accepted.
  • Port 443, 80, 88 or 8443.
  • A valid TLS certificate (TLS 1.2+). A self-signed certificate works only if you upload its public key.
  • Your endpoint must answer with HTTP 2xx quickly; otherwise Telegram retries and updates pile up.

Set the webhook online

  1. Open Telegram Bot Manager and paste the bot token from @BotFather.
  2. On the Webhook tab enter the URL of your handler.
  3. Press Generate to create a secret token and save it in your server config.
  4. Choose allowed_updates if you need only some update types (or chat_member / reactions, which are off by default).
  5. Press Set webhook. The status block shows the result immediately.

Parameters

ParameterWhat it does
urlHTTPS endpoint that receives updates as JSON POST requests.
secret_token1–256 chars A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -, sent in the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header of every request.
allowed_updatesUpdate types to receive. Empty list = everything except chat_member, message_reaction, message_reaction_count.
max_connectionsSimultaneous HTTPS connections, 1–100 (default 40).
ip_addressFixed IP to use instead of DNS resolution.
certificatePublic key of a self-signed certificate.
drop_pending_updatesDiscard updates that are waiting in the queue.

Same with curl

[[curl:setWebhook]]

With a self-signed certificate:

[[curl:setWebhookCert]]

Verify the secret token on your server

Always compare the header with your secret and reject other requests — the webhook URL alone is not a secret.

[[curl:verifySecret]]

Common errors

  • Bad Request: bad webhook: An HTTPS URL must be provided for webhook — use https://.
  • Bad Request: bad webhook: Webhook can be set up only on ports 80, 88, 443 or 8443 — change the port or put a reverse proxy in front.
  • Bad Request: bad webhook: Failed to resolve host — the domain has no public DNS record.
  • Bad Request: secret token contains unallowed characters — use only letters, digits, _ and -.

webhookInfo.title: Telegram getWebhookInfo Checker — Debug Your Bot Webhook
webhookInfo.description: Check your Telegram bot webhook online: URL, pending updates, last error message and what it means. Fix SSL, DNS, timeout and 4xx/5xx webhook errors.
webhookInfo.h1: Check a Telegram webhook with getWebhookInfo
webhookInfo.lead: getWebhookInfo shows whether Telegram can deliver updates to your bot. Here is how to read every field and fix the most common delivery errors.
webhookInfo.body:
Fields of WebhookInfo

FieldMeaning
urlCurrent webhook URL. Empty means the bot uses getUpdates (long polling).
pending_update_countUpdates waiting for delivery. A growing number means your server doesn't accept them.
last_error_date, last_error_messageTime (Unix) and text of the most recent delivery error.
last_synchronization_error_dateError while synchronizing updates with Telegram datacenters; usually temporary.
ip_addressIP address Telegram currently sends requests to.
max_connectionsMaximum simultaneous connections.
allowed_updatesSubscribed update types; absent means the default set.
has_custom_certificateWhether a self-signed certificate was uploaded.

Check with curl

[[curl:getWebhookInfo]]

Example response:

[[curl:webhookInfoResponse]]

Typical last_error_message values

  • SSL error {error:...:certificate verify failed} — incomplete certificate chain, expired or self-signed certificate. Install the full chain (fullchain.pem) or upload the self-signed public key.
  • Connection timed out / Read timeout expired — the server is unreachable or answers too slowly. Reply with 200 immediately and process the update in the background.
  • Connection refused — nothing listens on that port, or a firewall blocks Telegram's IP ranges.
  • Failed to resolve host: Name or service not known — DNS problem with your domain.
  • Wrong response from the webhook: 404 Not Found — wrong path in the URL or routing.
  • Wrong response from the webhook: 401 Unauthorized / 403 Forbidden — your server rejects the request, often because of a secret token mismatch.
  • Wrong response from the webhook: 500/502/503 — your handler crashes or the upstream behind the proxy is down. Check server logs.

After fixing

Refresh the status: last_error_date stays until the next error, so compare its time with the current one. If the queue contains outdated updates, drop them with drop_pending_updates.

deleteWebhook.title: How to Delete a Telegram Bot Webhook and Use getUpdates
deleteWebhook.description: Delete a Telegram bot webhook online (deleteWebhook), drop pending updates and fix “409 Conflict: can't use getUpdates method while webhook is active”.
deleteWebhook.h1: How to delete a Telegram bot webhook
deleteWebhook.lead: Remove the webhook to switch your bot back to long polling (getUpdates), to move it to another server or to stop a broken endpoint from piling up updates.
deleteWebhook.body:
When you need it

  • You run the bot locally with a library that uses getUpdates and see 409 Conflict: can't use getUpdates method while webhook is active; use deleteWebhook to delete the webhook first.
  • You are moving the bot to another server or domain.
  • The old endpoint is gone and Telegram keeps retrying.

Delete the webhook online

  1. Connect the bot with its token.
  2. Open Webhook → Danger zone.
  3. Tick Drop pending updates if you don't need the queued updates.
  4. Press Delete webhook and confirm.

Same with curl

[[curl:deleteWebhook]]

Then receive updates with long polling:

[[curl:getUpdates]]

Only clear the queue

To discard stuck updates but keep the webhook, use Drop pending updates: it calls setWebhook again with the same URL and drop_pending_updates=true. Enter your secret token so it is preserved.

Notes

  • deleteWebhook does not affect commands, profile or other settings.
  • Without drop_pending_updates the queued updates (kept for up to 24 hours) are returned by the next getUpdates calls.

botCommands.title: Telegram Bot Commands Editor — setMyCommands Online
botCommands.description: Edit Telegram bot commands online: setMyCommands per scope and language, deleteMyCommands, limits and format. Free, no code needed.
botCommands.lead: Bot commands appear in the menu and in hints when a user types “/”. You can set different lists for private chats, groups, administrators and languages.
botCommands.body:
Format

One command per line, the name and the description separated by a dash:

[[curl:commandsText]]
  • Up to 100 commands per list.
  • Name: 1–32 characters, lowercase English letters, digits and underscores. A leading “/” is removed automatically.
  • Description: 1–256 characters.
  • [ephemeral] marks commands whose answer is visible only to the sender (Bot API 10.2).

Scopes

ScopeWho sees the list
defaultEveryone, if no narrower scope matches.
all_private_chatsAll private chats.
all_group_chatsAll groups and supergroups.
all_chat_administratorsAdministrators of all groups.
chatOne specific chat (chat_id).
chat_administratorsAdministrators of one chat.
chat_memberOne member of one chat (chat_id + user_id).

Each scope can additionally have lists per language_code (two-letter ISO 639-1). Telegram picks the most specific scope, then the user's language, then the list without a language.

Same with curl

[[curl:setMyCommands]]

Delete a list:

[[curl:deleteMyCommands]]

Tips

  • Keep descriptions short — they are truncated in narrow menus.
  • Changes appear for users after the chat is reopened; clients cache the list.
  • Use the Menu button tab to show the command list or a Mini App on the button next to the input field.

hints.ssl: Certificate problem: install the full chain (fullchain.pem), renew an expired certificate, or upload the public key of a self-signed one.
hints.dns: Telegram can't resolve your domain. Check the DNS A/AAAA records, or set a fixed IP address.
hints.refused: Nothing accepts connections on that host and port, or a firewall blocks Telegram. Check the server and port.
hints.timeout: Your server is unreachable or too slow. Reply 200 immediately and process updates asynchronously.
hints.http3xx: Your endpoint redirects. Telegram doesn't follow redirects — use the final URL.
hints.http4xx: Your server rejects the request: check the URL path, authentication and the secret token check.
hints.http5xx: Your handler fails. Check the server logs and the upstream behind your reverse proxy.
